say.en: When a shop cuts the price of T-shirts from 500 rupees to 300, rupees people buy more. Today we turn this everyday fact into the law of demand. In this lesson: State the law of demand and the demand function.
Distinguish normal/inferior goods and substitutes/complements.
Distinguish movement along and shift of the demand curve; derive market demand.

title.en: Demand, demand curve and law of demand

body.en: Demand is the quantity of a good a consumer is willing and able to buy at a given price during a period. It depends on the good's own price, prices of related goods, income and tastes: $q = d(p, p_r, M, T)$. The *demand curve* shows quantity demanded at each price, other things constant. The law of demand: other things equal, quantity demanded falls when price rises and rises when price falls, so the demand curve slopes downward. A price fall makes the good relatively cheaper (substitution effect) and raises real income (income effect). A linear demand curve is $d(p) = a - bp$.

points.en: *Demand* function: q = d(p, pᵣ, M, T)
Reasons: substitution effect and income effect

narration.en: Demand depends on price, prices of related goods, income and tastes. The law of demand says price and quantity demanded move in opposite directions.

say.en: Law of demand: inverse price-quantity relation.
Reasons: substitution effect and income effect.
Here is the demand curve q equals 20 minus 2p. Price is on the vertical axis, quantity on the horizontal.
If price falls from 6 to 4, quantity rises from 8 to 12. We slide down the same curve: a movement along it.
If income rises for a normal good, more is bought at every price. The whole curve shifts to the right.
Own price moves us along the curve. Income, related prices and tastes shift the curve.

title.en: Normal and inferior goods; substitutes and complements

body.en: For a *normal* good, demand rises as income rises; for an inferior good (coarse cereals, for example), demand falls as income rises. Substitutes such as tea and coffee: a rise in the price of one raises the demand for the other. Complements such as petrol and cars: a rise in the price of one lowers the demand for the other. A change in the good's own price causes a movement along the demand curve; a change in any other factor shifts the whole curve.

narration.en: For normal goods demand rises with income; for inferior goods it falls. Substitutes compete; complements are used together.
narration.kn: ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಸರಕಿಗೆ ಆದಾಯ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿದಂತೆ ಬೇಡಿಕೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ; ಕೀಳು ಸರಕಿಗೆ ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಪರ್ಯಾಯ ಸರಕುಗಳು ಒಂದರ ಬದಲು ಇನ್ನೊಂದು; ಪೂರಕ ಸರಕುಗಳು ಜೊತೆಯಾಗಿ ಬಳಕೆಯಾಗುತ್ತವೆ.

Substitutes: p r ↑ gives demand ↑; complements: p r ↑ gives demand ↓.

body.en: *Market demand* is the total quantity demanded by all consumers in the market at each price. It is the horizontal sum of individual demand curves: at each price, add the quantities. If $d_1 = 10 - p$ and $d_2 = 15 - 2p$, then for prices up to ₹7.5 the market demand is $D = 25 - 3p$.

problem.en: Two consumers have demand curves d₁ = 10 − p and d₂ = 15 − 2p. Find the market demand curve and the market demand at p = ₹4.

steps.en: d₁ is positive for p < 10; d₂ is positive for p < 7.5.
For 0 ≤ p ≤ 7.5: D = (10 − p) + (15 − 2p) = 25 − 3p. For 7.5 < p ≤ 10 only consumer 1 buys: D = 10 − p.

answer.en: Market demand D = 25 − 3p (p ≤ ₹7.5), D = 10 − p (₹7.5 < p ≤ ₹10); at p = ₹4, D = 13 units.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Two consumers have demand curves d₁ = 10 − p and d₂ = 15 − 2p. Find the market demand curve and the market demand at p = ₹4.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Two consumers have demand curves d 1 equals 10 - p and d 2 equals 15 minus 2p. Find the market demand curve and the market demand at p equals 4 rupees.
d 1 is positive for p is less than 10; d 2 is positive for p is less than 7.5.

For 0 is less than or equal to p is less than or equal to 7.5: D equals (10 - p) plus 15 minus 2p equals 25 minus 3p. For 7.5 is less than p is less than or equal to 10 only consumer 1 buys: D equals 10 - p.
At p equals 4: d 1 equals 6, d 2 equals 7, D equals 13. Check: 25 minus 3 times 4 equals 13.

So the answer is Market demand D equals 25 minus 3p (p is less than or equal to 7.5 rupees), D equals 10 - p (7.5 rupees is less than p is less than or equal to 10 rupees); at p equals 4, rupees D equals 13 units.
